column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-rust.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS PINS. pleme-rust is a TIER-2 composer: 9 sibling jobs, each gated on
# `inputs.target == '<its own name>'`, no needs, no status functions. The whole
# contract is EXACTLY-ONE DISPATCH — one arm selects, the other eight skip — and
# that contract is invisible to every other layer. actionlint sees 9 valid
# expressions; unit tests see no code at all; a run where the wrong arm fired,
# or where none did, is a green tick either way. So every arm gets a row, and
# each row asserts the negative too: naming the other eight in expect-skip is
# what turns a duplicated or typo'd string literal into a finding instead of a
# second job quietly riding along.
# `inputs.target` is the ONLY context path any condition in this file reads, so
# it is the only key declared. Nothing here depends on the event, the actor, the
# repo's privacy, or an upstream job's outputs.
# THE TWO BOUNDARY ROWS, which are the ones that would otherwise rot:
#   unknown-target — a value matching no arm. This composer has no catch-all
#   and no default job, so an unrecognised target is a full no-op that reports
#   SUCCESS. That is intended (pleme.yml owns routing; a bad name is the
#   caller's bug, and failing here would just move the error one level away
#   from its cause) — but "intended" and "broken" render identically in the
#   Actions UI, which is the exact failure this whole layer exists for. Pinned
#   so that adding a catch-all later is a deliberate table edit, not a drift.
#   empty-target — target computed but empty: "detect ran and produced
#   nothing", a distinct state from any named type and from an unknown name.
#   `inputs.target` is `required: true`, which stops a caller OMITTING it but
#   does not stop one passing "". This is the row a future catch-all would
#   break on first, because a naive `else` arm fires on empty just as readily
#   as on a real miss.
# PUBLISH POSTURE. Eight of the nine arms dispatch to something that releases,
# publishes or pushes (the ninth, nix-devshell-cargo-test, only tests). There is
# no separate do-it / don't-do-it toggle to exercise: the don't-do-it input for
# any given publisher IS every other row in this file. Read the table as the
# claim that ONE call to pleme-rust can trigger AT MOST ONE publish path, and
# that a call carrying an unknown or empty target triggers NONE.
# LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: the linter evaluates this workflow as
# written and does not model reusable-workflow `with:`/`secrets:` propagation
# into a called workflow's own conditions. A row here asserts that the reusable
# was INVOKED, never that its internal jobs selected. Those leaves carry their
# own <workflow>.cases.tsv beside them.
cargo-auto-release
cargo-gate-ci
# Longest literal in the file, and a strict prefix-superset of no other arm —
# but `cargo-auto-release` IS a substring of it, so this row is what proves the
# dispatch matches whole strings rather than containing them.
cargo-publish-each-member-auto-release
# The only non-publishing arm.
nix-devshell-cargo-test
nix-image-auto-release
# rust-auto-release / rust-binary-auto-release / rust-binary-release / rust-release
# are four near-identical names differing by one segment. They are the arms most
# likely to be crossed by a copy-paste edit, and the four rows below are the
# only thing in the repo that would notice.
rust-auto-release
rust-binary-auto-release
rust-binary-release
rust-release
# BOUNDARY: no arm matches. Whole workflow no-ops and reports success, on purpose.
unknown-target
# BOUNDARY: target computed but empty. Distinct state from unknown-target.
empty-target
